question: Advertising in the US is a $150 billion business. What bigger business does Peter Thiel say founders overlook?
answer: Selling: in Thiel’s figures, the US sales industry takes in about $450 billion a year, three times advertising, mostly out of sight. Poor sales, he argues, sink more start-ups than poor products do: an invention with no good way to reach buyers is a bad business, however clever.
move: Ask how a thing will reach its buyers as early as how it works.
simply: You bake the best cake in town and keep it in a box under your bed. Nobody tastes it. Telling people about the cake is part of running a good cake shop.
why: The same holds for a job application, a research paper or a charity appeal. Good work rarely spreads by itself; treating the effort to reach people as part of the work, not a vulgar extra, often decides whether it gets used at all.
source: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, Zero to One, 2014
reference: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future (Crown Business, 2014), ch. 11, If You Build It, Will They Come?
